LESSON: THINGS IN OUR SCHOOL

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Our School
Topic 5.2: Things in Our School
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Things in Our School, part of Our School in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we have schools? 2. Why do we have play materials at school?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Things in Our School together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: learner develops concepts of uses of things found at school when modelling them.

Values:
• Patriotism: learner develops sense of nationalism when colouring the National flag.

• Responsibility: learners develop accountability when using things found in school properly.

91

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Financial literacy: learners learn to use economic resources properly as they use things found in school.

Link to other learning area:

National flag in school can be used to learn colours in Creative Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Realia-things found at school such as National flag, Video clips, charts, name cards, and pictures and picture cut outs about

things found at school, theme-based multi-purpose Communication Board, adapted digital devices, songs and poems about

things found at school, universal cuffs with padded pencils, crayons with grips, slant boards, foot-boards for learners using

lower extremities, book holders and page turners, positioning/ seating devices whose worktops/ table tops are at a suitable

height, mobility devices such as wheelchairs/ crutches, head/ mouth pointers, splints for hands/ hand stabilizers,

Related Service Providers: Physiotherapist, Occupational Therapist, Learner Support Assistant/ Scribe
